key_insight: High calculation accuracy did not guarantee reliable error detection in MedPhysBench, a benchmark of medical physics tasks.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark tests calculations and checking tasks relevant to radiation safety, but does not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Ten seeded generators cover radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, nuclear medicine and radiation protection.
Protocol-based code supplies reference answers, with unit conversion and tolerance-based grading.
Paired checking tasks present a colleague’s worksheet or result, balanced between correct answers and single planted errors.
evidence_signal: Across 12 models on a held-out split of 1,200 items, calculation scores ranged from 33.3% to 100.0%; five models detected at least 96.7% of mostly large planted errors with at most 4% false alarms.
watch_item: Two shielding-item problems were found after evaluation; four of nine answers graded incorrect among the top four models followed NCRP Report 151 where benchmark items were misstated or ambiguous.
paper_title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection
